subject.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention

question: Must synchronous exec-approval decisions remain ordered behind every policy write, or may they intentionally use the last committed policy while a same-process write is active?
rationale: That choice determines whether the repair should implement reentrant snapshot access or permit stale reads across an authorization update; automation should not select that security contract.

options.title: Preserve serialized authorization
options.body: Implement process-local reentrancy or committed-snapshot handoff so readers never bypass an active policy writer.

options.title: Permit last-committed reads
options.body: Explicitly define stale committed policy as acceptable during writes and prove that every persistence fallback exposes only complete snapshots.

options.title: Pause this approach
options.body: Close or redesign the PR if neither ordering contract can be implemented without another lock or policy source of truth.

recommendation.title: Preserve serialized authorization
recommendation.body: Implement process-local reentrancy or committed-snapshot handoff so readers never bypass an active policy writer.
